key_insight: A non-iterative federated spectral method learns shared latent patient representations across institutions without pooling patient-level EHR records.
clinical_relevance: In stroke EHR data, the learned representations highlight clinically distinct patient subgroups, though benefits for care decisions remain untested.
method: Each institution shares aggregate marginal frequencies and a low-rank spectral summary while retaining patient-level records locally.
A central server combines summaries to recover shared representation components and their normalization.
Theoretical analysis provides row-wise recovery guarantees and error bounds under explicit regularity conditions.
evidence_signal: Simulations closely matched pooled analysis and outperformed single-site and existing federated benchmarks; multi-facility stroke EHR data demonstrated interpretable subgroups.
watch_item: Keeping records local does not by itself guarantee privacy; shared summaries require disclosure-risk assessment.
paper_title: Communication-Efficient Federated Learning of Latent Patient Representations from Multi-Institutional EHRs
